root_causes.description: The checkout service exhibits an isolated server-side p99 latency spike (up to ~1950ms) while every peer service remains under ~26ms. No errors, CPU/memory pressure, or pod restarts accompany it, so the latency is injected/in-process rather than caused by resource exhaustion or a failing dependency.

evidence.observed_value: checkout p99 latency: mean=409.88ms, p95=1564.97ms, p99=1872.99ms, max=1950ms
evidence.expected_baseline: peer services p99 < 26ms (frontend 24.96ms, product-catalog 9.59ms, shipping 4.64ms); expected checkout p99 well under ~50ms
error_rate < 0.01; confirms latency fault is not an http_abort/error storm

evidence.observed_value: 6 traces, 0 errors, p95_duration=600000ms; slow spans incl. trace 1ff36341ec76075e 'user_checkout_multi' 1244ms, trace fdf8ee413977048c 47776ms, trace 1365d01214772724 10140ms
evidence.expected_baseline: checkout spans normally tens of ms with 0 errors

evidence.observed_value: checkout cpu_usage: mean=0.003, max=0.004 cores (no anomaly)
evidence.expected_baseline: no CPU spike; rules out cpu_stress

evidence.observed_value: checkout memory: mean=24.56MB, max=24.95MB (flat, no anomaly)

root_causes.description: Alternative interpretation: latency is introduced on one of checkout's downstream egress calls (cart, payment, email, shipping, currency, product-catalog). However all downstream services show normal p99 (<10ms) and zero errors, so a pure downstream failure is not supported.

evidence.observed_value: payment p99=1.980ms; shipping p99=4.534ms; product-catalog p99=9.591ms; cart p99=1.980ms (all normal)
evidence.expected_baseline: downstream p99 < 10ms — no downstream latency to propagate

root_causes.description: Upstream frontend calls checkout, so a checkout slowdown could surface at the frontend. But frontend p99 is flat at ~25ms with no errors/restarts, so it is a symptom boundary rather than the origin.

remediation_steps: Confirm the latency fault on checkoutservice: check any chaos/flagd fault injection targeting checkoutservice in otel-demo and disable/revert it.

Inspect the slow checkout spans (e.g. user_checkout_multi ~1.2s, order-consumed ~10-48s) to identify the internal stage introducing the delay (e.g. injected network/latency delay vs. a slow blocking call).
Since CPU/memory/restarts/errors are all normal, rule out resource scaling and focus on injected delay removal; re-measure checkout p99 to verify return to <50ms.
Add/verify a p99 latency SLO alert scoped per-service so latency regressions on a single service are caught even when upstream/downstream peers look healthy.
